title: Lumbar intervertebral joint coupled/principal displacement ratios, intact, single principal loads
condition: intact, no preload, nucleus pressurised to 626 kPa

quantity.name: coupled/principal displacement ratio Gamma_ij
quantity.definition: mean over increments and specimens of (incremental coupled displacement / incremental principal displacement); upper and lower bounds across specimens given as max/min. Cells left blank in the paper (no significant coupling) are omitted. Load/displacement coordinate system with origin O_L at the intersection of the disc mid-transverse plane and the line joining the two vertebral body centres (NOT the vertebral body centre); Z along that centre line (axial compression +Fz), Y in the plane of symmetry (antero-posterior, +Fy anterior shear), X lateral (+Fx right lateral shear); rotations G (flexion-extension about X), B (lateral bending about Y; CCW = -B), A (axial rotation about Z; CW = +A). Lower member fixed, upper member unconstrained (loads by pulleys/dead weights).

source.authors: Tencer AF, Ahmed AM, Burke DL
source.sample: 14 lumbar intervertebral joints (L2-3 and L4-5) from 8 cadavers (7 M, 1 F); human cadaveric lumbar joints, disc grade 1-2, radiographically normal except one hypoplastic L5

protocol.summary: Max principal loads (Table 3): 90 N right lateral/anterior/posterior shear, 823 N axial compression, 11.2 Nm flexion and extension, 14.7 Nm CCW lateral bending, 12.9 Nm CW axial torque; applied in 3 ~equal steps (readings 1 min after steps 1-2, 2 min after step 3). Nucleus pressurised to 626 kPa by water injection before testing (simulating reclining in vivo pressure); 4 conditioning cycles of +-axial torsion at max torque.
how_to_simulate: Model an L2-L3 or L4-L5 joint; fix the lower vertebra; define the load/output point at the disc centre O_L (mid-disc on the line joining the vertebral body centres), Z along that line
Pressurise/pre-stress the nucleus to ~0.63 MPa if the model allows (paper injected water to 626 kPa); no external preload
Apply each principal load alone in 3 equal steps to 90 N shear, 823 N compression, 11.2 Nm flexion/extension, 14.7 Nm lateral bending, 12.9 Nm axial torque, upper vertebra otherwise free
Compute the ratio of each coupled displacement increment to the principal displacement increment (displacements at O_L) and average; compare sign and range (bounds) rather than exact value
protocol.notes: Coordinate system: Load/displacement coordinate system with origin O_L at the intersection of the disc mid-transverse plane and the line joining the two vertebral body centres (NOT the vertebral body centre); Z along that centre line (axial compression +Fz), Y in the plane of symmetry (antero-posterior, +Fy anterior shear), X lateral (+Fx right lateral shear); rotations G (flexion-extension about X), B (lateral bending about Y; CCW = -B), A (axial rotation about Z; CW = +A). Lower member fixed, upper member unconstrained (loads by pulleys/dead weights). Coupled translations under torques depend on the reference point (O_L at disc centre). Only force-load coupling found: A-P translation with axial compression.
